To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the evaluation measures of cluster stability and purity are not suitable for evaluating stream clustering algorithms.

1) the performance of stream clustering algorithms is dependent on both the evaluation measure and the data distribution, and 2) evaluation measures for cluster quality are sensitive to the data distribution and the clustering algorithm.

1. the clustering performance of algorithms on evolving data streams is highly dependent on the evaluation measure and 2. there is no single best evaluation measure, but a set of evaluation measures that should be used together for a comprehensive assessment of clustering performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
(i) assessing the quality of clusterings, (ii) comparing different clustering algorithms, and (iii) evaluating the performance of the different algorithms and measures on evolving data streams.
the following aspects: - A comprehensive evaluation of state-of-the-art algorithms and evaluation measures on evolving data streams.

the following aspects: (1) The MOA environment is extended with new stream clustering algorithms, (2) the performance of these algorithms is assessed using a set of evaluation measures, (3) the evaluation measures are visualized using a new interactive visualization tool, (4) the MOA environment is used to compare the performance of the different algorithms and evaluation measures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of the clustering algorithm is highly dependent on the evaluation measure used.
the performance of the evaluated algorithms is strongly dependent on the evaluation measures.
there is no one best stream clustering algorithm, but the best algorithm depends on the data and the evaluation measure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a novel framework to assess stream clustering algorithms and evaluate their quality using different evaluation measures.
we present a novel, open-source framework for the experimental comparison of stream clustering algorithms.
we provide an open source software environment for the evaluation and visualization of stream clustering algorithms, and we offer a set of evaluation measures for cluster evaluation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the framework can serve as a starting point for researchers and practitioners to evaluate and compare different clustering algorithms or evaluation measures on real-world data streams.
we show how to compare the performance of stream clustering algorithms with each other and with respect to evaluation measures.
the framework allows for the evaluation of the algorithms in terms of the quality of the clusterings they produce.
